entries.title: Finite population effects on epigenetic reproductive isolation

source.question_paraphrase: Finite population models may magnify the relative strength of epigenetic barriers to gene flow; this is not a universal monotonicity conjecture.

entries.narrowed_target: For an exactly specified finite two-deme life cycle, compare epigenetic and matched genetic neutral-marker transmission at fixed horizon, or separately fixation probability; find parameter conditions or exact small-population counterexamples.
prior_art: Published deterministic diploid two-deme two-locus recurrence and haploid constant-transition spectral solution
Fogarty and Otto 2024, DOI 10.1073/pnas.2322885121, already studies finite-population gene-culture effects; exact comparison remains required
Related 2026 methylation/signalling association work DOI 10.1098/rstb.2025.0024 does not settle the finite stochastic comparison from its inspected abstract
existing_assets: Retained source audit and source-life-cycle reading
Affinity-model fixed-point and exponential-fixation results, which concern a different recurrence and are not this open direction
entries.next_step: Confirm the primary conclusion and define the life cycle before exact rational enumeration of the smallest nontrivial population transition matrix.

entries.title: Identifiability and transport of cellular perturbation responses
entries.status: CONFIRMED SOURCE QUESTION; narrowed target CANDIDATE

source.locator: Theoretical Framework: Connection to Causal Transportability, Definition 3.1 and Proposition 3.2; Context Problem and Why Implicit Context Inference Fails
source.access: PubMed-indexed preprint; named sections inspected within first 28000 of 33728 body characters
source.question_paraphrase: Under which assumptions can source-context interventional information identify a causal perturbation effect in a target cellular context?

entries.narrowed_target: For a finite context-indexed causal model class and fixed response query, characterize compatible response values and the additional context/perturbation measurements needed for identification or a specified interval width.
prior_art: Established causal transportability theory; generic mechanism-shift impossibility is not new
scPILOT 2026, DOI 10.1002/advs.77461, transfers previously observed perturbations across contexts; its abstract does not justify arbitrary unseen mechanism transfer
CausCell and scCausalVI provide assumption-dependent representation/perturbation approaches requiring exact estimand comparison
existing_assets: Omnibus distinction between available targets C_A(D), compatible models V(D), and response set R_q(D)
Existing predictive-state and stochastic abstraction interfaces as supporting assets, not cellular empirical models
entries.next_step: Compare one exact finite transport contract with source-cited prior theory and scPILOT partitions; test its information requirement with a tiny observationally equivalent model pair before training.
